title: Limb segment masses (ISB joint-centre segments), male and female

quantity.name: segment mass
quantity.definition: segment mass relative to body mass

source.authors: Dumas R, Chèze L, Verriest JP
source.sample: 77 living subjects (31 M from McConville 1980; 46 F from Young 1983) – secondary analysis; US adults (McConville et al. 1980 males; Young et al. 1983 females), stereo-photogrammetric body surface reconstruction
source.age: M mean 27.5 y; F mean 31.2 y
source.notes: M: mean 80.5 kg, 1.77 m; F: mean 63.9 kg, 1.61 m. Corrigendum doi 10.1016/j.jbiomech.2006.07.016 (Head & Neck values corrected).

protocol.summary: Limb segment masses complementing the torso/pelvis/head values.
how_to_use: Use with anthropometry.dumas2007.trunk_mass so the whole body sums consistently (bilateral limbs counted twice).
COM and inertia of limbs are in Table 2 of the paper (not transcribed here).

measurement.method: stereo-photogrammetry (surface volumes, uniform density 1 g/cm³), adjusted to ISB segment coordinate systems

protocol.notes: SCS: Torso Y-axis LJC->CJC (cranial), Z normal to LJC-CJC-SUP plane pointing laterally (right), X = Y×Z (anterior); origin CJC. Pelvis: Z LASIS->RASIS, Y normal to ASIS-MPSIS plane pointing cranially, X = Y×Z; origin LJC. Head & Neck: Y CJC->HV, origin CJC. LJC/HJC from Reed et al. 1999. Torso = Thorax + Abdomen of the original data (C7/CJC to LJC, i.e. ~L5/S1), Pelvis = LJC to HJC level – boundaries are joint-centre based, unlike de Leva/Pearsall.

extraction.check_notes: All values re-read from the rotated 200-dpi image of Table 2 (p.548) and the corrigendum table (p.1651). OCR had dropped minus signs (e.g. alternative pelvis CoM Y -5.0/-14.9); image values used. Head & Neck values replaced by corrigendum values. Corrigendum prints Head & Neck CoM X as +1.6/+2.0 % although its landmark table gives CoM X = -4/-6 mm (i.e. ≈ -1.6/-2.2 %) – sign as printed, flagged.

pass_rule.rule: input data – not graded; use for robustness checks
